`_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` creates its temp root as a top-level side effect (`const tmpRoot = fs.mkdtempSync(...)` at the module's harness section), but only `runTests` removes it. Any process that imports the module without running a suite leaks an empty `/tmp/sandbox-boot-*` directory — and the exam does exactly that on every run: Proof leg (a)'s `node -e "import('./fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs')..."` export-check imports and exits, leaving one behind each time. The inline original had no such path (module load was the run), so this is a small regression introduced by turning the rig into an importable module. Creating the root lazily on first `makeHome` fixes it and keeps the runner's failure path (which may never call `makeHome`) correct.; `_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs:302` creates `tmpRoot` eagerly at module load (`const tmpRoot = fs.mkdtempSync(...)`) but only `runTests` removes it (line 481). In the original single-file exam, importing the module *was* running the exam, so the pairing was total; after the extraction any consumer that imports the helper without calling `runTests` leaks an empty temp directory — including the task's own first Proof command, whose `node -e "import('./fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs')..."` export check imports and exits. Advisory only: nothing in the Claim or the exam depends on it, and both test files do call `runTests`. If you want it tightened, make the root lazy so it is only created by the first `makeHome`:

  let tmpRoot = null
  const root = () => (tmpRoot ??= fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'sandbox-boot-')))

with `makeHome` using `root()` and `runTests` doing `if (tmpRoot) fs.rmSync(tmpRoot, ...)`.; concern: plan-defect: Proof leg (b) requires the string `the evidence branch` to be absent from fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_edges.mjs, but a pre-existing prose comment inside section 7 (originally line 1188, 'and it rides to the evidence branch, which is the only artifact...') carries that exact string. completenessFindings.detail: Plan-level Claim and Global Constraint 3 ("No sim under `fleet/tests/` spawns `node` on another `test_*.mjs`: the strings `execFileSync('node'` and `spawnSync(process.execPath` occur in no `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs` whose argument names a sibling `test_` file") fail against the integrated tree. `fleet/tests/test_deadline_slack.mjs:66` binds `const WORKER_SPEC = path.join(HERE, 'test_run_worker.mjs')` and `fleet/tests/test_deadline_slack.mjs:98` runs `spawnSync(process.execPath, [WORKER_SPEC], { cwd: ROOT, env, encoding: 'utf8' })` — the constraint's exact literal string, with a sibling `test_` file as its argument. The loop at lines 101-108 executes it twice (slack unset and `FLEET_TEST_SLACK=1`), each time asserting `test_run_worker.mjs` exits 0 and prints `ALL TESTS PASSED`. That is the duplicated bridge item the plan's Goal targets: `tests/test_fleet_suite.py:5` already collects `test_run_worker.mjs` as its own parametrized item, so its wall-clock is paid three times per suite run. This is not covered by any task's Files (tasks 1-3 own `test_run_engine_examiner.mjs`, `test_run_engine_proposed_patch.mjs`, `test_run_engine_exam_edits.mjs`, `test_sandbox_boot*.mjs`, `_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs`, `test_roles_examiner.mjs`) and is named nowhere in the plan — the Goal and Task 1 Context enumerate only three re-running sims (`test_run_engine_examiner.mjs`, `test_run_engine_proposed_patch.mjs`, `test_exam_edited_patches.mjs`). It is a survey gap in the plan, not a regression introduced by this run — the file is untouched and at BASE — but the plan's headline Claim ("After this run no fleet sim re-runs another sim as a subprocess") is false of the delivered tree, and no per-task referee could have seen it from a single diff. A full sweep of `execSync|spawn\(|fork\(|execFile\(|execFileSync\(|spawnSync\(` across every `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs` confirms this and `test_exam_edited_patches.mjs` are the only two remaining; all other call sites spawn `bash`, `git`, `python3`, `doctor.mjs`, the confine hook, or `node -e` inline scripts.

Plan-level Claim ("After this run no fleet sim re-runs another sim as a subprocess") is also unmet by `fleet/tests/test_exam_edited_patches.mjs:201-207`, which loops over the four `FROZEN` entries (`test_run_engine.mjs`, `test_run_engine_fixloop.mjs`, `test_run_engine_cap_width.mjs`, `test_run_engine_proposed_patch.mjs`) and runs each with `spawnSync('node', [path.join(here, name)], { cwd: REPO_ROOT, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 300000 })`, asserting exit 0 and the sentinel. Unlike the `test_deadline_slack.mjs` case this is explicitly and deliberately scoped out: Task 1's Context states "The third sim that re-runs siblings, `test_exam_edited_patches.mjs`, is the concurrent judging-waste plan's file (its digest legs go there), so after both plans merge no sim under `fleet/tests/` re-runs another." The mechanical form of Global Constraint 3 is also not tripped — the literal here is `spawnSync('node'`, neither of the two strings the constraint names. Worth an issue only to record that the plan's Claim is contingent on the concurrent plan landing, not satisfied by this run alone; the coordination this run did owe it was done correctly (the re-frozen digest for the modified `test_run_engine_proposed_patch.mjs` is in place at `fleet/tests/test_exam_edited_patches.mjs:194` and the driver's full-suite run is green).
